segments.text: When you ask an AI a question, it first calculates what your words mean together,
but then it faces an entirely different problem. How does it actually begin forming a reply?
Let's give the AI a simple prompt. What should I name my new dog?
To make this process easy to follow, we are going to look at each individual word as a single token.
An AI cannot instantly output a fully formed thought. To write anything at all,
it requires a specific mathematical anchor point to launch its response.
This graphic shows the four steps that happen before the answer begins.
The AI breaks the question into tokens, marks their positions, assigns starting vectors,
and updates those numbers by passing them through layers.
AI uses the final token's updated numbers to predict what comes next.
This diagram shows why that specific token matters. Sitting at the end of the row,
it gathers contextual information from every single token before it.
In this prompt, the question mark is the final token.
AI uses its vector to predict the first token of its answer.
The final punctuation mark functions as a mathematical container,
holding the compressed context of the entire prompt to launch the response.
With the context gathered, the AI is ready to answer.
It takes the updated numbers from that final token and uses them to calculate a probability
score for every possible token in its entire vocabulary.
This kicks off a strict repeating cycle.
The AI selects a winning token, adds it to the existing reply,
and then uses that newly expanded text to make its next prediction.
What looks like typing on your screen is actually a continuous mathematical loop,
calculating probabilities, adding a piece, and recalculating based on the new whole.
This chart details that prediction process.
Look at prediction one on the left. The context anchor is still that question mark.
The AI selects you from the top predictions.
Moving to the center, this process repeats three more times, sequentially adding could,
name, and him. Instead of drafting the entire sentence in advance,
the model builds its preamble one piece at a time,
constantly shifting its context window forward with every new addition.
By prediction five on the right, the reply so far is you could name him.
The word him becomes the new final token.
Looking at the updated top predictions, we see spot, max, and buddy.
The AI selects spot, completing the sentence. You could name him spot.
By continuously updating the context, the mathematical probabilities naturally shift away
from generic sentence starters and toward the highly specific nouns you requested in the prompt.
You might wonder why the AI didn't just spit out a dog name immediately,
since that's exactly what you asked for. Instead, it began with you, a standard conversational opening.
Each added token changes what can fit next.
A specific dog name only becomes a highly probable continuation
after the contextual runway of you could name him is firmly established in the output.
AI keeps predicting tokens until it produces a special token that signals the answer is finished.
The AI doesn't know the complete idea it is going to express before it starts typing.
The final response reveals itself dynamically as the growing context narrows the mathematical
possibilities. This infographic shows the formal structure of how AI builds an answer.
Reminding ourselves of the setup, you ask for a dog name, and the answer generated so far is
you could name him. In step one, rank. The AI scores every possible next token.
This results in spot at 22%, max at 17%, and buddy at 14%.
Moving to steps two, pick, and steps three, add. The AI selects a next token, in this case spot,
and attaches it directly to the growing answer. Finally, in step four, repeat, the AI takes this new
longer context and uses it to predict again, asking what the subsequent token should be.
Inference is the process AI uses to generate an answer one token at a time.
AI thinking is a recursive high-speed microcycle of ranking, picking, adding, and repeating.
Let's bring this down to two core takeaways. The entire response is constructed sequentially,
piece by piece, and this complete cycle of generation is known as inference.
